implementation_notes: Diesel gives a record its own persistence through derives rather than a base class: a struct with #[derive(Queryable, AsChangeset, Identifiable)] (and Insertable) maps to a table declared by the table! macro, and the guide states that foo.save_changes(&conn) is equivalent to diesel::update(&foo).set(&foo).get_result(&conn). What replaces the classic structure is the compile-time DSL - the schema is Rust code, so a column rename breaks the build instead of the request - and the connection is passed explicitly, which keeps transaction scope visible. Choose it for synchronous services that want the SQL checked at compile time.
pitfalls: save_changes writes every AsChangeset column rather than only the changed ones, so partial updates need an explicit update(...).set(...) with a narrower changeset struct.
The table_name must match the table! declaration or the derive fails at compile time; the primary key also has to be named id unless overridden with diesel(primary_key(...)).
Diesel connections are not Send-shareable: a threaded server must pool them (r2d2/deadpool) and pass one connection per request, or the record API becomes the bottleneck.

variants.name: SeaORM ActiveModel with async insert/update
variants.implementation_notes: SeaORM splits each table into a read model (Model) and a write model (ActiveModel) whose fields are ActiveValue::Set/NotSet; an ActiveModel inserts itself (pear.insert(db).await, returning the stored row) and updates itself from its primary key, so the object still owns its persistence but the async runtime is the execution model. What replaces the classic structure is the Set/NotSet distinction: unlike a mutable struct, an ActiveModel can say 'leave this column alone', which removes the partial-object overwrite class of bugs. Choose it for async services where the database client must not block the executor.
pitfalls: Default::default() leaves every field NotSet, so a hand-assembled model that forgets a Set silently skips that column - the mirror image of the null-overwrite bug.
update() requires the primary key to be Set; an ActiveModel built from request data must carry the id explicitly.
The async DatabaseConnection is cheap to clone but must be pooled/owned per task; holding it inside a struct that is then shared across tasks invites executor stalls.
